source.title_en: Floods and landslides bring a sea of suffering to the Dawei region

facts.forecast_multiple: >3x the rain on other days this month
facts.cause: A low-pressure area moving in from Thailand over the Tanintharyi coast
facts.context: Environmental destruction across the region, including hills cut away and streams wrecked by mining, is being blamed for making the disaster worse, as a strong El Niño sets in.

A landslide at Min Yat Chaung, west of the village, buried houses. A mother and her child were buried; rescuers recovered the mother's body and found the child alive.
Listed among villages between Dawei and Launglon hit by flooding and landslides.

Hillsides collapsed and water in the village stood about a person's height deep, trapping people in their homes. Rescue teams that left Dawei early on 27 Sep only reached Tha Byar, at the entrance to Launglon town, around midday.

The worst-hit township. Flooding and landslides struck the town and more than 20 villages. Tens of people are dead or missing, including children. Three bodies had been recovered in the township by the afternoon of 27 Sep; houses in the tens were buried and people in the tens were still missing.
sites.dead_note: Township total by 27 Sep afternoon; the same three deaths are also listed at Kadet Nge (2) and Min Yat (1).

A village hemmed in by hills and the sea. From about 5 pm on 26 Sep landslides buried houses and people. A child and a man are missing. Slides were still coming down on the morning of 27 Sep, so no rescue was possible, and contact with the village was lost around midday.
Landslides hit the village. Deaths are reported but not yet confirmed.
Near Maungmagan beach, north-west of Launglon. Listed among villages hit by flooding and landslides.

Landslides on the night of 26 Sep and the morning of 27 Sep buried about 30 houses and carried away two-wheel tractors and motorcycles. No one was hurt. About 30 households, more than 60 people, moved to the monastery and other safe places and need help.

sites.text: Record rainfall. Drains overflowed and main roads went under water in some wards. Elderly people and children trapped in their homes were brought out by social welfare groups. Water covered the road in front of a private hospital on Ka Myaw Kin road, and strong wind brought down at least five large trees. Homes flooded in places that had never flooded before.
The checkpoint at Pauk Taing bridge, at the entrance to Dawei, marks the northern end of the flooded stretch that runs south past Pe Det.

timeline.en: Heavy rain sets in from the morning.
Landslides begin burying houses and people at Kyauk Ni Maw.
Night: floodwater overtops roads and pours into homes. People move out in the dark. Village-to-village roads are cut the same night.
Night into morning: landslides bury about 30 houses at Kayin Gyi.
Morning: the ground floors of houses in Kin Shey are under water.
Early morning: rescue teams set out from Dawei for Launglon.
DMH records 11.02 in (280 mm) at Dawei, a new record. The old record was 9.68 in.
Landslides are still coming down across Launglon and the rain is still heavy. Rescuers urge people by streams and hillsides to move to safety.
Midday: contact with Kyauk Ni Maw is lost.
Midday: the rescue teams reach Tha Byar at the entrance to Launglon.
About 2:30 pm: the Poe Zar Pin landslide between Launglon and Nyin Maw stops the rescue teams heading south.
From 3 pm strong winds sweep the whole of Dawei District; rain does not let up.
Afternoon: three bodies recovered in Launglon Township. Tens of people still missing.
Evening: rain continues over most of Dawei town. Water enters compounds that had never flooded before.
Forecast: heavy rain continues across Tanintharyi through 28 Sep, easing but still strong.
